decision_text.source: cmos strategic_decisions, the longest row of 1,933
decision_text.value:
s105-m04 MISSION-START AUDIT (4 axes captured BEFORE any code per Rule 1; n=11 of the audit pattern). IMPLEMENTATION path expected — no D-memo fork — but mission-spec scoping requires an explicit framing decision on the agent-callable surface (no existing MCP tool wraps the three C5 emitters; only review.resolve from s103-m01 is a tool today).

(a) PREVIEW SHAPE for JSON artifacts. Chosen: STRUCTURED PANELS with a "Show raw JSON" toggle per panel.
- review-queue card: summary metric tiles (entitiesTotal, flaggedCount, tierCounts.high/medium/low/unknown) + entries list (one row per entity: urn, tier badge, score, elementName/elementType, lowest signals as score-tagged chips).
- conflict-detail accordion: one per flagged entry — full signals sorted ascending as a score-tagged list, evidence gaps list with source-kind chip ('signal' / 'evidence_refs' / 'confidence_decomposition'), optional context block (projectionVariants, brandOverlay, schemaorg) when present.
- apply-summary card: decisionCounts metric tiles (accept/patch/defer/dismiss), defaultActionUsed callout, matchedPolicyIds chip list, entries list (urn + decision badge + reason + policyId).
- Each panel includes a "Show raw JSON" toggle that swaps the structured view for the pretty-printed `code` field. Matches mission spec axis (a) recommendation: helps an orchestrating agent reason about both shape (structured) and full fidelity (raw).
- Rejected: (A) tree view (interactive expand/collapse over arbitrary JSON — useful for unstructured inspection but loses the artifact-specific affordances that make the queue/detail/summary distinct), (B) syntax-highlighted JSON only (no reasoning surface — readers can already pretty-print).

(b) CHAIN COMPOSITION UX. Chosen: STEP-THROUGH with action buttons (three steps revealed sequentially).
- Initial state: fixture picker + policy radio + "Step 1: Generate Review Queue" button. No panels rendered.
- After step 1: queue card revealed; "Step 2: Resolve via Policy Bundle" button enabled.
- After step 2: resolutions list rendered alongside queue card; conflict-detail accordion under each flagged entry; "Step 3: Generate Apply Summary" button enabled.
- After step 3: apply-summary card rendered. "Reset" button appears to start a fresh chain.
- Progress dots / step counter at top of the view (1 → 2 → 3 with active highlighted).
- Honest framing note: server returns all artifacts in a single review.chain call; client-side progressive reveal is a presentation choice that mirrors the agent's actual sequential workflow. A one-line UI note ("Artifacts rendered from a single review.chain call; in production an orchestrating agent invokes the queue + resolve + summary steps as discrete tool calls") will appear under the step counter to keep Rule 12 honesty (no implied serialization that isn't actually there).
- Rejected: (A) all-at-once layout (more demo-efficient but loses pedagogy; the chain's whole point is that each step's output is input to the next), (B) wizard/modal flow (too heavy for an inspection surface).

(c) review.resolve POLICY-BUNDLE INPUT. Chosen: DEFAULT POLICY BUNDLE HARD-WIRED with a 2-option radio for comparison.
- Default: `flag-below-0.5` bundle from the s104-m04 Q3 e2e fixtures (matches `score < 0.5` → defer). Labeled "Policy: flag-below-0.5 (defer items with score < 0.5)".
- Alternative: `dismiss-all` bundle (catch-all → dismiss). Labeled "Policy: dismiss-all (dismiss every item)".
- Bundle bodies live as constants in the playground source — agents and humans reading the code can see the exact bundle shape.
- Each label includes a one-sentence inline subtitle explaining the bundle's effect.
- NO policy-editor UI per post-C4-drop discipline and mission spec axis (c) recommendation. Toggling the radio between bundles lets users observe matched-policy vs default-action paths without any editor surface.
- Rejected: (A) policy-bundle editor (C4-shaped UI-build-ahead-of-signal — we dropped C4 in this sprint for exactly that reason), (B) bundle-from-file upload (path-traversal surface, no real demo win over a 2-bundle radio).

(d) FIXTURE SOURCING. Chosen: Q3 FIXTURES via the existing `fidelity.preview` FIXTURE_PATHS server-side allow-list (reused; not duplicated).
- The 9 Q3 fixtures (user/product/subscription + content/article/author/comment + content-pack + billing-multi-entity + subscription-low-confidence) are already exposed by `fidelity.preview`'s allow-list and exercise the full range of `confidence_decomposition` shapes that the C5 chain reasons over.
- Stage1 fixtures are intentionally NOT extended with confidence_decomposition per memory ([project_stage1_v17_status]) — Stage1 emission rarely includes it, and backfilling synthetic decomposition values would be inauthentic.
- Recommended demo trio per success criterion: `subscription-low-confidence` (canonical flagged case — 1 defer entry under flag-below-0.5), `article` (all-high, exercises default-action path), `content-pack` (3 entities, mixed decisions across bundles).
- Implementation: refactor `fidelity.preview.ts` to EXPORT its FIXTURE_PATHS map; new `review.chain.ts` imports + reuses it. Single source of truth for the playground fixture allow-list.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN rooted in axes:
1. Server: extract FIXTURE_PATHS from `src/tools/fidelity.preview.ts` into a shared module `src/tools/playground-fixtures.ts` (or export from fidelity.preview directly). Single source of truth, reusable by review.chain.
2. Server: new MCP tool `review.chain` at `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/review.chain.ts`. Input: `{ fixture: string, policies: PolicyBundle, options?: { reviewThreshold?, lowestSignalsN?, evidenceGapThreshold? } }`. Output: `{ queue: ReviewQueueArtifact, resolutions: EvaluationResult[], auditTrail: AuditTrail, conflictDetails: Array<{ urn: string, detail: ConflictDetailArtifact }>, summary: ApplySummaryArtifact, diagnostics: { fixture, fixtureSource: 'allow-list', policyBundleId? } }`. Bundle validation reuses `validatePolicyBundle` from review-policy.
3. Server: JSON schemas at `src/schemas/review.chain.input.json` + `src/schemas/review.chain.output.json` (closed, additionalProperties:false at every level). Output schema composes existing queue/conflict-detail/apply-summary schemas via $ref + adds chain-level diagnostics.
4. Server: registration in `src/index.ts` toolSpecs + `src/tools/registry.ts` fallback + `src/tools/registry.json` auto array.
5. Server: unit test at `src/tools/review.chain.test.ts` covering: (i) trio × 2 bundles success paths, (ii) decision/policyId one-for-one mapping, (iii) unknown-fixture error (OODS-RC-001), (iv) invalid-policy-bundle error (re-thrown from review.resolve).
6. Playground: add `runReviewChain(...)` helper in `bridge-client.ts` returning a typed result.
7. Playground: new view "Reconcile" as a third tab alongside Compose/Stage1 (hash `#reconcile`). Components:
   - `ReconcileView.tsx` — orchestrator (fixture picker + policy radio + step state machine + result rendering).
   - `ReviewQueuePanel.tsx`, `ConflictDetailPanel.tsx`, `ApplySummaryPanel.tsx` — each with raw-JSON toggle.
   - Reuse `FixturePicker` from m02 for fixture selection.
8. Manual smoke: trio × 2 bundles in dev mode (bridge + playground); confirm tsc + lint clean on both packages.

OUT OF SCOPE per mission spec: A2UI runtime emitter UI surface; concordance integration UI; the 9 Vite URL transform cleanup (carried as passive watch); live-bridge automated smoke (manual smoke only per s102-m02 precedent — bridge usually not running, and Rule 12 honesty over fabricated coverage). Telemetry/OTLP tracing of review.chain is implicit via the m01 dispatcher span — no additional code needed for the I3 tracing tie-in beyond the existing telemetry layer.

OPTION-(C)-AS-SINGLE-CALL framing acknowledged: an alternative was three separate MCP tools (review.queue, review.conflictDetail, review.applySummary). Chosen single review.chain tool over the three-tool surface per Rule 2 (Simplicity First) — the chain IS the unit of meaning, and the step-through UX is purely a presentation choice. Agents wanting the discrete steps already have review.resolve as the policy-evaluation surface; the emitters are pure functions and the chain tool composes them deterministically. If real-world usage signal later shows agents need to invoke the queue or summary alone, three-tool decomposition becomes an additive follow-on.
